Each stack is a JSON file with exactly 5 `questions` that tell one linked story. Players can tap a lifeline to see 4 choices: the correct answer plus 3 hand-written wrong answers that you will write.

- src/data/stacks/back_to_the_future.json

- src/data/stacks/character-name-origins.json

TASK: For each of the 5 entries in each file's top-level `questions` array, add a field `"choices": ["...", "...", "..."]` with exactly 3 WRONG answers. Place it immediately after `acceptedAnswers`. Do NOT add choices to `deeperMode.questions`. Do NOT change any other field, text, order, or formatting (keep 2-space JSON), EXCEPT: in the five kids/ files only, also add a top-level field `"choicesByDefault": true` (put it right after `description`) so young players see the choices automatically. The easiest safe way is a small `node -e` script that parses the JSON, inserts keys in the right order by rebuilding objects, and writes back with JSON.stringify(data, null, 2) + '\n'. See the finished reference example in src/data/stacks/van-gogh.json.

REFERENCE (Van Gogh):
- 'Who painted The Starry Night?' (Vincent van Gogh) -> ["Paul Gauguin", "Claude Monet", "Paul Cézanne"]
- 'How many paintings is he said to have sold?' (One) -> ["Three", "Twelve", "None"]
- 'Title of that painting?' (The Red Vineyard) -> ["The Sower", "Sunflowers", "The Potato Eaters"]
- 'Who bought it?' (Anna Boch) -> ["Theo van Gogh", "Paul Gauguin", "Dr. Paul Gachet"]
- 'How much did she pay?' (400 francs) -> ["50 francs", "1,000 francs", "2,500 francs"]

RULES FOR GREAT DECOYS (this is what makes the game fun):
1. Definitely wrong. Never an alternate correct answer, a looser version of the right answer, or anything in acceptedAnswers. If the fact is genuinely disputed, avoid decoys from the disputed side.
2. Same type and format as the canonical `answer`: a year gets years, a number word gets number words, a person gets people of the same field/era, a place gets places of the same kind. Match capitalization style and rough length.
3. Tempting to someone who half-knows the topic: real names, real places, real works from the same world (common misconceptions are ideal). For the kids stacks, keep decoys friendly and recognizable to a 7-10 year old (e.g. real dinosaur names, real planets, real animals) but still clearly wrong. No jokes, no 'All of the above', no made-up nonsense.
4. Never use the answer to ANY other question in the same stack (it would spoil the story).
5. Avoid near-spellings of the correct answer (e.g. for '400 francs', '4,000 francs' is graded as a typo-match and will be rejected). For numbers, spread values out.
6. Each choice at most 50 characters; 3 distinct choices.

VERIFY: after editing each file run `node tools/stackLint.js <file>` from the app folder. It must print 'Stack passes validation' with no warnings. If it reports a choice would be graded correct or spoils another level, replace that choice. Do not run git commands. Do not edit any files other than your 11 stack files.

WHILE YOU WORK, also act as a fact-checker: if you notice a question, answer, or explanation that is factually wrong or seriously misleading, do NOT change it; just report it.

FINAL RESPONSE: (a) confirm all 11 files pass stackLint, (b) list any facts you think are wrong or shaky with file, level, and a one-line reason with a source if you know one.

_**Agent (default)**_

**(a)** All 11 files pass `node tools/stackLint.js` with "Stack passes validation" and no warnings. Each of the 5 main questions has 3 wrong answers in `choices`, placed right after `acceptedAnswers`. The five kids files also have `"choicesByDefault": true` right after `description`. `deeperMode.questions` was not changed.

- I checked beforehand that rewriting each file with 2-space JSON keeps the existing formatting exactly, so the only changes are the new fields.
- One decoy failed the linter at first: "Neverland Ranch" in Hero's Journey, level 5. It would have been graded correct because `"the ranch"` is an accepted answer, so I replaced it with "American Zoetrope".

**(b) Facts that look wrong or shaky** (none were changed):

- **`philip-k-dick-super.json`, level 4:**
  - The question says amphetamines "fueled paranoia until" the 1974 vision, but Dick had largely quit amphetamines after his 1972 rehab at X-Kalay in Vancouver (Sutin, *Divine Invasions*).
  - Dick described a "pink beam of light," not a laser.
- **`philip-k-dick-super.json`, level 3:** Dick was a heavy amphetamine user in the 1960s, but "relied on" them specifically to write *Androids* is more than the sources show. "Testing empathy while writing" is also an odd way to put it.
- **`jesus-historical-mythic.json`, level 5:** The Magi never announce euangelion ("good news"). In the Gospels, the angel brings the "good news" to the shepherds (Luke 2:10). The story link here is misleading.
- **`jesus-historical-mythic.json`, level 4:** Matthew only says "magi from the east." Calling them Babylonian is one reading; tradition more often makes them Persian or Median.
- **`jesus-historical-mythic.json`, level 3:**
  - "Many scholars cite" overstates it. The Jupiter–Saturn conjunction (Kepler's idea) is one theory among several, including a Jupiter–Venus conjunction in 3/2 BCE, a comet or nova, and Molnar's 6 BCE occultation. Many historians treat the star as a literary device.
  - The triple conjunction was in 7 BCE, not "7–6 BCE."
- **`jesus-historical-mythic.json`, level 2:** Yeshua is a Hebrew name, a short form of Yehoshua, that was also used in Aramaic. "Literally means in Aramaic" is loose wording.
- **`heroes-journey-super.json`, level 4:** That Lucas read Campbell while drafting *Star Wars*, and that the story follows the monomyth "beat for beat," is disputed. Kaminski's *The Secret History of Star Wars* argues the Campbell influence was largely stressed after the fact.
- **`heroes-journey-super.json`, level 5 explanation:** I couldn't verify "five of the six episodes" or "Campbell's last two summers."
  - Filming took place in 1985–86 at Skywalker Ranch and the American Museum of Natural History.
  - Campbell died in October 1987, so "last two summers" would mean 1986–87, which doesn't match.
- **`character-name-origins.json`, level 4 (low confidence):** The note "Gandalf was originally chief Dwarf (= Thorin)" may be misattributed. The Hobbit drafts were edited by John D. Rateliff in *The History of The Hobbit*, not by Christopher Tolkien.
- **`back_to_the_future.json`:**
  - At level 2, `acceptedAnswers` includes `"1"` and `"one"`, so a bare "1" scores as correct. That's a data issue rather than a factual one.
  - At level 4, Marty also plays guitar on "Earth Angel" at the dance, so the question is slightly ambiguous. I kept "Earth Angel" out of the decoys for that reason.
